title: Post-Market Surveillance for AI: Designing a Technical Monitoring System Analogous to FDA MedWatch

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: post-market surveillance is a structurally missing governance component; designing an AI analog with a prototype data schema directly addresses this gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: analyzing MedWatch's design and translating it to AI is a structured analytical task, manageable with guidance but requires understanding two domains.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: analyzing MedWatch, designing a schema, and prototyping signal detection with simulated data spans multiple components but has clear milestones.

novelty.reasoning: Partially addressed: post-market surveillance for AI medical devices is well-studied, but a general-purpose MedWatch analog for all AI deployments is less developed.

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: The FDA has active research on post-market monitoring of AI-enabled medical devices (OSEL program). Nature published 'A general framework for governing marketed AI/ML medical devices' (npj Digital Medicine, 2025). PMC published 'Methodology for Conducting Post-Marketing Surveillance of Software as a Medical Device Based on AI Technologies' (2023). The FDA Digital Health Advisory Committee discussed a central database for generative AI monitoring. The Paragon Institute published on targeted post-market surveillance for AI. However, these focus on AI within medical devices. The broader proposal — designing a general-purpose MedWatch analog for all AI deployments (not just medical) with a data schema and signal detection — extends beyond existing work. The medical device space is well-covered; the general AI deployment surveillance system is partially novel.
